claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced plastic strain relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr has enhanced toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing conditions.
The enhanced plastic strain and toughness of WTaTiVZr are governed by coherent nanoprecipitates.
The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy contains coherent nanoprecipitates.
Commercial pure tungsten lacks the coherent nanoprecipitates proposed for WTaTiVZr.
Testing both materials at approximately 800 °C under matched processing and heat-treatment conditions would isolate the effect of coherent nanoprecipitates.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitate interfaces relieve stress concentrations that can cause premature crack initiation.
Facilitated dislocation transmission and reduced stress concentration improve plastic deformation.
Facilitated dislocation transmission and reduced stress concentration improve fracture toughness.
Dislocation motion is more hindered in pure tungsten than in nanoprecipitate-containing WTaTiVZr.
At high temperature, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater tensile plastic strain than pure tungsten.
At high temperature, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
The coherent nanoprecipitates remain stable up to approximately 800 °C.
The proposed benefit may cease at extreme temperatures or under loading modes that destabilize the precipitate structure.
Coherent-nanoprecipitate engineering in tungsten-based refractory alloys can improve tensile ductility while retaining high strength.
The quantitative improvement and optimal precipitate size, density, and coherence in WTaTiVZr are unknown pending experimental validation.
